fields.h1: Build an SEO Client Questionnaire Your Strategist Can Act On

fields.features_heading: Where the Answers Go After a Client Submits
fields.features_subheading: A question list gets the facts down. Emergent builds the questionnaire and the client record your strategist works from.
fields.feature_1:
Questions that follow the client type

Ask first whether the client is a local business, an online store, or a software firm. A local business gets questions about offices and service areas, and a store about its catalog.
fields.feature_2:
An access checklist instead of passwords

List each tool the strategist needs, such as Search Console and Analytics. The client ticks each one after adding the strategist as a user, and nobody types a password into a form.
fields.feature_3:
Competitors and keywords as sortable rows

Ask for up to 5 competitors, each with a website address, plus the search terms the client thinks buyers type. Each entry is its own row, so the strategist can sort and compare them.
fields.feature_4:
Risky answers go to a senior strategist

Ask whether the site has ever had a manual action or worked with another agency. A Yes sends the senior strategist a Slack message with the answer before the kickoff call is booked.
fields.feature_5:
Answers that become the kickoff agenda

Once the questionnaire comes in, the app turns the answers into an agenda for the first call: the client's goals, its competitors, any missing access, and any past penalty.
fields.feature_6:
Client records and code you keep

Every questionnaire is a row in a database you own, with no response cap. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and keep building on it wherever you host it.

fields.tab_content_1:
Four services at each of 3 offices, 12 pages

Aldwick Family Dental runs 3 offices, and its office manager picks Local business on Kestrelgate Search's questionnaire. The form asks for each office's address and the services patients search for. She lists 4, including implants and emergency visits. The record shows 12 office-and-service pairs to plan pages around.
fields.tab_content_2:
Vantwell's catalog comes in ranked by revenue

Vantwell Tea sells loose-leaf tea online, and its founder answers on her phone between orders. As an online store, she is asked for the number of product pages, the 3 categories that earn the most, and the month sales peak. She reports 1,240 product pages, oolong ahead of green and black, and a November peak.
fields.tab_content_3:
One missing access item, chased after 2 days

Selwick Roofing finished every question on Monday. Its access checklist shows Kestrelgate added as a user in Search Console and Analytics, but not yet as a manager of the Business Profile. Two days later, on Wednesday, the app emails Rhea Wickerly, Selwick's marketing lead, a link to the 1 item still missing.
fields.tab_content_4:
Before kickoff, Zarek knows of the 2024 penalty

Brindlecombe Bikes ticked Yes to "Has your site ever had a manual action?" and added that it came in 2024, after a previous agency bought links. The app messages Zarek Bexleigh, Kestrelgate's senior strategist, in Slack with that answer. The penalty also goes first on the kickoff agenda.

fields.howto_title: How to Create an SEO Client Questionnaire
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to an SEO client questionnaire that puts missing access and past penalties in front of the strategist before kickoff.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Write down what the strategist needs
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Split the questions by client type
fields.howto_step_1_des: List what the strategist needs before the first call: goals, competitors, target searches, and the tools to be added to. Leave anything off that list out of the questionnaire, because each extra question is one more reason a client stops halfway.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Pick the client types you sign most often, such as local businesses and online stores. Put the business type question first. A local client then sees office and service questions, and a store sees catalog questions in their place.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Name each tool the strategist works in, Search Console and Analytics among them, and ask the client to add the agency as a user. Only a Search Console property owner can add users, so the client may need to forward that request.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Save the rest for the kickoff call. Use short choices where they fit, such as a list of months for the sales peak, and keep open text for goals and for the story behind any past penalty.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Write one prompt with the client types, the questions each one sees, the access checklist, and who hears about which answers. Emergent builds the form, a record for each client, and a dashboard listing every client and its missing access.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Decide which answers need a person right away. A reported manual action might message the senior strategist in Slack, while missing access waits 2 days and then emails the client. Everything else stays in the client record until kickoff.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Fill it in as a fake client
fields.howto_step_7_des: Submit the questionnaire twice under test names, once as a local business and once as a store, and tick Yes to the manual action question on one. Check that each saw its own questions and that the strategist got the Slack message.

faq_plan.q: What is an SEO client questionnaire?
faq_plan.a: An SEO client questionnaire is the set of questions an agency or consultant sends a new client before work starts. It collects the business type, goals, competitors, target searches, past SEO history, and which tools the client can grant access to. The strategist then starts the kickoff call with facts in hand.

faq_plan.q: How do I create an SEO client questionnaire?
faq_plan.a: Describe it to Emergent's AI form builder in one prompt. Name the kinds of clients you take on, the questions each kind answers, the tools you need access to, and who gets alerted about which answers. Emergent builds the questionnaire, a database of client records, and a dashboard, and you change any part of it by prompting again.

faq_plan.q: What questions should an SEO client questionnaire include?
faq_plan.a: Cover five areas: the business and what it sells, goals and how success is measured, customers and competitors, the site's history, and access. History means past agencies and any penalty. Access means which tools the client has added you to. Then add questions that apply only to that client's type, such as office locations for a local business.

faq_plan.q: How far before the kickoff call should an SEO client questionnaire go out?
faq_plan.a: Send it at least a few days before the kickoff call, as soon as the contract is signed. The answers can then shape the agenda. If you already send a general client onboarding questionnaire, add the SEO questions to it instead of sending a second form that asks for the company details again.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should an SEO client questionnaire have?
faq_plan.a: Aim for about 20 and cover the rest on the kickoff call. Offer choices wherever a list will do, such as business type or the month sales peak, and save open text for goals and history. Emergent can build the questions to branch by client type. A store owner then never scrolls past questions written for a dental office.

faq_plan.q: Should an SEO questionnaire ask clients for their passwords?
faq_plan.a: No. Ask the client to add you as a user in each tool, and list those tools in the questionnaire with a checkbox each. In Google Analytics, the person adding you needs the Administrator role at the account or property level. Ask the client who on their side holds it.

faq_plan.q: Can one SEO client questionnaire work for local businesses and online stores?
faq_plan.a: Yes, as long as the first question asks for the business type and the questions after it depend on the answer. Each client skips the other type's questions, which keeps the form short. The same branching suits an interior design questionnaire, where the room being redone decides what comes next.

faq_plan.q: How can an SEO client questionnaire uncover a past penalty?
faq_plan.a: Ask in the questionnaire, then open the Manual actions report in Search Console once you have access. Google issues a manual action when a human reviewer finds pages that break its spam policies, and it notifies site owners in that report and in the Search Console message center. Ask for the year and the cause as well.

faq_plan.q: What should I do with SEO client questionnaire answers before kickoff?
faq_plan.a: Turn them into the agenda. Put risks first, such as a past penalty or missing access, then goals, then competitors and target searches. In an app Emergent builds, each submission is saved to a database you own, and the app can lay out the agenda from that record. Nobody copies answers by hand.

faq_plan.q: What does an SEO client questionnaire ask that a design brief does not?
faq_plan.a: It asks about search: the terms buyers type, the competitors that show up in results, the site's history, and tool access. A logo design questionnaire asks about style and where the logo will appear. If a client needs both, send them as separate forms so each set of answers reaches the right person.
